title: [DBIP] Split security executionEnvironment into executionEnvironments (runtimes) + languages (array of langs), normalize separators
body:
### Proposal type
Split column (one conflated column -> two typed columns) + add validation

### Affected scope
- Canonical: `references/offers/security.csv`
- Per-network security listings: `listings/specific-networks/<network>/security.csv`
- `schema.json` on json-tools (replace `executionEnvironment` with two array columns + enum constraints)
- Security wiki page

### Motivation / problem statement
At main, `security.csv` has 92 rows. The `executionEnvironment` column **conflates two orthogonal dimensions** in a single free-text field:

1. **Execution environment / runtime** — `EVM`, `SVM`, `WASM`, `Substrate`, `Solana`, `Aptos`, `EOS`, `Fabric`
2. **Programming language** — `Solidity`, `Move`, `Cairo`, `Vyper`, `Rust`, `Go`

Measured distribution (92 rows): empty(31), `TBD`(18), `EVM`(15), `Solidity`(6), `Solidity, Move, Cairo, Vyper, Rust`(4), `Rust`(4), `EVM (Solidity)`(3), `EVM, SVM, WASM`(3), `EVM (Solidity), Rust, ZK`(1), `EVM, Substrate, Rust`(1), `EVM (Solidity/Vyper)`(1), `Solidity, Cairo, Rust, Go`(1), `EVM, Rust, Move, Solana`(1), `Solidity, Vyper`(1), `EVM, Solana, Aptos, EOS, Fabric`(1), `EVM (Solidity, Vyper)`(1).

Concrete defects:
- **8 rows mix both dimensions** (e.g. `abdk`, `certik`, `certora-gambit`, `chainsecurity`, `chimera`, `halmos`, `quantstamp-audit`, `statemind-smart-contract-audit` all carry both a runtime and a language in one cell).
- **Inconsistent separators**: 6 rows use parenthetical qualification `EVM (Solidity)` while others use comma `EVM, SVM, WASM` — the same fact (EVM + Solidity) is encoded two different ways, so it is un-queryable ("which tools support Solidity on EVM?" cannot be answered by a single filter).
- `TBD`(18) and empty(31) are placeholders, not environments.

### Proposed change
1. **Split** `executionEnvironment` into two typed array columns:
   - `executionEnvironments` — array of runtimes from a closed enum: `evm`, `svm`, `wasm`, `substrate`, `solana`, `aptos`, `eos`, `fabric`, ...
   - `languages` — array of languages from a closed enum: `solidity`, `move`, `cairo`, `vyper`, `rust`, `go`, ...
2. **Normalize** to comma-separated arrays, drop parenthetical qualifiers (e.g. `EVM (Solidity)` -> `executionEnvironments=["evm"]`, `languages=["solidity"]`).
3. **Add enum constraints** in `schema.json` so future free-text cannot creep back in.
4. **Null semantics**: `TBD`/empty mean **not verified**; MUST NOT default to "EVM only".

### Relationship to #3697 / #3678
#3697 renames the *sdks* `sdk` column to `sdkLanguages`; #3678 normalizes *oracle* `dataTypes`. This DBIP is the security-table companion that splits its conflated `executionEnvironment` — distinct table, distinct column, not a duplicate.

### Payout address
USDC payout address (Chain-Love DBIP bounty): `0x0751C1d8DbA83d8968401293b50Bc91E7701dcf8`

title: Solidity build helper includes excluded contracts on Windows and leaves cwd changed on failure
body:
## Summary

At commit 045a6efd11b353385686730ac5c71ea134983dd3, the Solidity build helper uses slash-based regex filters against native Windows paths. As a result it includes vendored contracts under lib, test contracts under tests/integration and tests/solidity, and previously copied sources under contracts/solidity/precompiles.

`RELATIVE_TARGET` is also interpolated as a native Path into a regex. On Windows the resulting backslashes are interpreted as regex escapes, and the existing `test_is_ignored_folder` assertion for `abc/contracts/solidity/precompiles` already fails.

Separately, `compile_contracts_in_dir` changes the process working directory before validating hardhat.config.js or running npm/Hardhat. Each error path raises before restoring the directory. Expected: preserve the caller's cwd after success and failure.

A focused patch normalizes paths for matching and restores cwd in finally. Eight selected assertions fail before the fix; the full helper test file passes all 12 cases afterwards, including real npm installation and Hardhat compilation on Windows/Python 3.14.7. The 11 offline cases also pass on Linux/Python 3.11. The fixes affect build tooling, with no remote exploit or bounty eligibility claimed.

title: Bounty API: accept smart-wallet (EIP-1271) creator signatures on PATCH /jobs/:id/public-submissions
body:
## Goal

A bounty whose creator is a smart-contract wallet (a Coinbase Smart Wallet such as a Verdikta agent's CDP wallet, or a Base Account) can toggle its `publicSubmissions` flag through the existing creator-signed `PATCH /api/jobs/:id/public-submissions` flow.

## Context

`verifyPublicSubmissionsAction` in `example-bounty-program/server/utils/messageAuth.js` checks the signature with `ethers.verifyMessage` (ecrecover) and compares the recovered address to `job.creator`. A contract wallet has no private key of its own, so no signature can ever recover to its address: every toggle attempt by a smart-wallet creator gets a 401.

Observed on Base mainnet, bounty 101 (2026-09-28): the owner asked the agent that created it to make submissions public, and the agent had no way to do it. The creator `0xA3b423861e6D6501a05e87d1f500fFff2402f7B1` is an ERC-1967 proxy to the Coinbase Smart Wallet v1.1 implementation `0x00000110dCdEdC9581cb5eCB8467282f2926534d`. Every agent-created bounty has a smart-account creator, so no agent can ever use this path today. Human creators using Base Account on the website are probably affected in the same way (not verified).

The standard fix is EIP-1271: when the creator address has code, call `isValidSignature(hashMessage(message), signature)` on it and accept the magic value `0x1626ba7e`. The agent-side counterpart (signing with the smart account and calling this endpoint) is tracked in verdikta/verdikta-agents (linked below).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When `job.creator` has contract code, the verifier accepts the signature if `creator.isValidSignature(hashMessage(message), signature)` returns `0x1626ba7e`, called through the server's configured RPC provider.
- [ ] EOA creators are verified by ecrecover exactly as today, with no change in behavior.
- [ ] Existing rejections are unchanged: wrong signer, Bounty ID mismatch, body/message value mismatch, and an expired or future timestamp return the same status codes as today.
- [ ] An `isValidSignature` call that reverts or returns anything other than the magic value is rejected with 401, never 500 and never accepted. An RPC failure never results in acceptance.
- [ ] Every caller of the verifier awaits it (it becomes async).
- [ ] `/api/docs` and `agents.txt` say the signature may be an EOA `personal_sign` or an EIP-1271 smart-wallet signature.
- [ ] Deployed to testnet, then mainnet.

## Validation

- Unit tests: an EOA signature passes; a contract creator with a mocked `isValidSignature` returning the magic value passes; non-magic, revert and RPC-error cases get 401 or another non-2xx response and are never accepted.
- Testnet: a signature produced by a CDP smart account (from the verdikta-agents counterpart, or a script using viem `toCoinbaseSmartAccount(...).signMessage`) toggles the flag, and `GET /api/jobs/:id` reflects the new value.
- Mainnet: the agent that created bounty 101 sets `publicSubmissions: true`, and `GET /api/jobs/101` shows `true`.

## Scope

In scope:

- `messageAuth.js` verification, the PATCH route's call site, and the docs/agents.txt text.

Out of scope:

- ERC-6492 (undeployed wallets): every bounty creator has already sent `createBounty`, so its wallet is deployed.
- Website UI changes.
- Agent-side signing (verdikta-agents).
- Any other creator-authorized endpoint.

title: [Feature]: verification gated release policy for auth-capture (a pact-escrow profile)
body:
### Problem or use case

auth-capture deliberately defines the hold and stays silent on the release: capture or void is a discretionary act of the captureAuthorizer. That's the right layering, but it leaves the two parties with no protocol-level way to (1) agree upfront what satisfactory delivery means for this payment, (2) verify delivery against that agreement, and (3) dispute a wrong release decision. Today the client trusts the captureAuthorizer's judgment, off-protocol.

That blocks the use case several open issues are circling: agent-to-agent task delegation where payment releases on verified completion (#1247), dispute handling when verification is contested (#2001), a correctness and dispute layer for what settlement can't see (#2887), and canonical delivery proof at settlement (#1195, #2833).

Concrete example: an agent pays $195 for a data cleaning job under auth-capture with autoCapture:false. What decides capture vs void? Today, nothing the counterparties agreed to in a machine checkable form. The acceptance tests passing or failing should be that decision, and both sides should have committed to those tests before work started.

### Proposed solution

A release-policy profile over auth-capture. No changes to the scheme itself, the profile specifies what a conformant captureAuthorizer executes:

  1. Before authorization, buyer and seller co-sign a Verifiable Task Contract: a JSON object fixing task scope by hash, price, verification method, challenge window, and the seller's bond. Canonicalized with JCS (RFC 8785), signed with JWS (RFC 7515).

  2. Release becomes mechanical. Verification passes: capture. Verification fails: void. On the optimistic path, capture fires at challenge-window expiry unless a fraud proof lands; the bond funds slashing, challenger cost reimbursement, and a capped bounty, because slashing alone doesn't fix the verifier's dilemma. Verification is graded per contract: deterministic re-execution, TEE attestation (EAT/RATS), zkML, or staked arbitration.

  3. At settlement, both parties co-sign a Work Attestation carrying the contract hash and outcome: a delivery receipt in the sense #1195 and #2833 are after, except only emittable through a bonded, escrowed contract, which is what makes accumulated receipts expensive to fake.
 
The full lifecycle is specified as an IETF Internet-Draft, draft-laxsharma-pact-00 (individual submission, Experimental). One honesty note: Section 8 of the -00 currently expresses the x402 binding as a standalone pact-escrow scheme, written against the escrow and deferred lineage that was closed in May (#873, #426). Reshaping that binding into a profile over the merged auth-capture machinery is exactly the change I'd make in -01, and this issue is me proposing it here first. Schemas and worked examples whose hashes verify in CI: https://github.com/pact-spec/spec . Draft: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-laxsharma-pact/

Concrete ask: (a) is this better shaped as a profile doc under specs/schemes/auth-capture/ or an extension under specs/extensions/? (b) If maintainers see a path, I'll draft that spec doc as a PR. It's a -00, published to be demolished; sharp edges welcome.

title: security: a private channel for vulnerability reports (SECURITY.md, GitHub reporting, HackerOne Community Edition)
body:
After the release. Today there is no way for a researcher to report a vulnerability in yarilo privately: no `SECURITY.md`, no private reporting on the repository, no program on any platform. Checked on 2026-10-02: YesWeHack and Intigriti have no free tier for open source; huntr closed its open-source program in June 2026; HackerOne's Community Edition is a free full subscription for OSI-licensed, non-commercial projects; GitHub private vulnerability reporting is free on public repositories.

## What to do

1. **`SECURITY.md` in the repository root.** Supported versions (the release line), where to report (the GitHub form below, then the HackerOne program once accepted), what to expect: first answer within one week, fix and advisory before public disclosure, no bounty promised. English, short.
2. **GitHub private vulnerability reporting** on `yarilomail/yarilo`: Settings → Advanced Security → Private vulnerability reporting → Enable. Reports arrive as draft advisories; a CVE is requested from the advisory. Repository admin does this.
3. **Apply for HackerOne Community Edition** (https://www.hackerone.com/company/open-source-community). Conditions, all met or one day of work: OSI licence, project older than three months with shipped releases, `SECURITY.md` in the root, a link to the HackerOne program in the navigation of doc.yarilomail.org, first response to a report within one week. The subscription is free; a 5% processing fee applies only to bounties actually paid, and paying is optional.
4. **Public docs**: a "Security" page on doc.yarilomail.org (repository `yarilomail/documentation`) with the same content as `SECURITY.md` and the program link in the site navigation, since HackerOne requires the link there.
5. **Decide on bounties later**: start with no bounty table; revisit after the first real reports.

## Not in scope

A paid platform (YesWeHack, Intigriti, Bugcrowd managed tiers): no public pricing, sales-led, nothing that the free options above do not give at this stage.

## Done when

`SECURITY.md` is on `main`, the GitHub reporting form is live on the repository, the HackerOne program is accepted and linked from the docs site, and a test report through each of the two channels reached the maintainers.

## Overview
Build a responsive, modern Kanban board application integrated with the Algorand blockchain. The platform allows users to manage project tasks through columns (To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done) while enabling task creators to attach ALGO bounties held in smart contract escrow, which are released to assignees upon verified task completion.

## Scope
- **Frontend Kanban Application:** Next.js (React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS) with drag-and-drop column support (`@dnd-kit`).
- **Algorand Wallet Integration:** Multi-wallet support (Pera, Defly) using `@txnlab/use-wallet-react` for signing transactions and user identity.
- **Smart Contract (Escrow):** AlgoKit-based smart contract (PyTeal or TEALScript) deployed to Algorand TestNet that holds ALGO bounties and releases funds to the assignee or refunds the creator.
- **Task Data Persistence:** Database integration (PostgreSQL with Prisma or Supabase) to store boards, columns, task metadata, and on-chain transaction IDs.
- **On-chain Action Flows:** Lock bounty on task creation, assign task to connected wallet, and release bounty on moving to 'Done' approved by creator.

## Out of scope
- MainNet deployment (MVP targets Algorand TestNet).
- Support for custom ASA tokens (native ALGO only for MVP).
- Complex multi-sig or DAO governance dispute mechanisms.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] User can connect/disconnect Algorand wallets (Pera and Defly) on TestNet.
- [ ] Kanban UI supports creating boards, adding columns, and creating/editing/moving task cards.
- [ ] Task creators can specify an ALGO bounty that triggers an escrow deposit transaction.
- [ ] Task assignees can claim or be assigned tasks using their Algorand wallet address.
- [ ] Moving a task to 'Done' allows creator approval to trigger contract escrow release to the assignee's address.
- [ ] Database correctly tracks task state, wallet addresses, and transaction hashes.
- [ ] Automated tests cover smart contract logic and critical API endpoints.

# Smart Contract Risk Scorer

## Purpose
Analyze smart contracts for security vulnerabilities and rug pull indicators to protect users from malicious tokens and scams in the DeFi ecosystem.

## Specification

**Job:** Analyze a smart contract and return comprehensive security assessment with risk score, vulnerabilities, and actionable recommendations.

**Inputs:**
* `contract_address` - Smart contract address to analyze (0x...)
* `chain` - Blockchain network (ethereum, polygon, arbitrum, optimism, base)
* `scan_depth` - Analysis depth: "quick" (30s) or "deep" (2-3 min)

**Returns:**
* `risk_score` - Overall risk score (0-100, higher = more risky)
* `risk_level` - Risk category: "low", "medium", "high", "critical"
* `vulnerabilities[]` - List of detected security issues with severity
* `security_checks` - Results of all security validations (honeypot, ownership, proxy detection)
* `external_checks` - Third-party API verification results (GoPlus, Token Sniffer)
* `contract_info` - Contract metadata (name, creator, age, verification status)
* `recommendations[]` - Actionable security recommendations
* `confidence` - Confidence level of the analysis (0.0-1.0)

## Acceptance Criteria

✅ Analyzes smart contracts for security risks and rug pull indicators  
✅ Multi-source verification (Etherscan + GoPlus + Token Sniffer APIs)  
✅ Detects honeypots, hidden ownership, and malicious code patterns  
✅ Source code analysis for verified contracts (50+ malicious patterns)  
✅ Bytecode analysis fallback for unverified contracts  
✅ Ownership analysis (renounced, timelocks, multi-sig detection)  
✅ Risk score calculation with confidence level  
✅ Detailed findings with evidence and severity ratings  
✅ Response time < 10 seconds for quick scans, < 30 seconds for deep scans  
✅ Must be deployed on a domain and reachable via X402

## Use Cases

- **Before investing:** Check if a new token is a scam or rug pull
- **Portfolio audit:** Analyze existing holdings for security risks
- **Due diligence:** Verify contract safety before interacting with DeFi protocols
- **Whale watching:** Detect concentrated ownership and creator holdings
- **Honeypot detection:** Identify tokens that cannot be sold

## Done When

Agent provides accurate security analysis with verified risk assessments from multiple data sources, helping users make informed decisions about smart contract interactions.

Before beginning work on the bounty, you must submit a proposal. Only if your proposal is accepted will you be able to claim the reward of the bounty. *In particular for this bounty you need to detail the testing you will use other than unit testing.*

There should be at most 1 week between proposal is accepted and you start working on the bounty. It should take you at most 1 month to complete the bounty.

For this bounty you will need to rewrite the [voting contract](https://github.com/near/core-contracts/tree/master/voting) into AssemblyScript making sure that they have the same API.

With the new addition of `includeBytes` function in AssemblyScript, near-sdk-as should have enough parity with near-sdk-rs that the core smart contracts should be able to be written in AS. The trickiest part of the contracts are the cross contract calls. Rust provides a high level abstraction for working with promises. For an example for batch promise calls in AS see the [sdk's repo here](https://github.com/near/near-sdk-as/blob/master/assembly/__tests__/sentences.ts).
